timeline.event: Per Okene's 2023 BBC Outlook account (via BBC Mundo), the tug had spent the previous day working hard in storm-roughened seas, stabilising a tanker at a Chevron loading point.

The anchor-handling tug Jascon 4 (owner West African Ventures, part of Sea Trucks Group, under contract to Chevron Nigeria) capsized and sank while on 'tension/static tow' of a tanker loading at Chevron's Single Buoy Mooring #3, about 15 nautical miles (about 30 km) off Escravos, Delta State. It settled upside down on the seabed at about 30 m. Okene, the cook, was in a toilet. He gave 04:50 to Reuters in 2013 and 'ten to five' to the BBC in 2023. AP and the Guardian/AP text say 'around 4:30 a.m.' (DISPUTED: 04:30 vs 04:50; prefer 04:50, his own repeated figure).

Chevron Nigeria statement: initial reports say heavy ocean swells caused the capsize. Emergency response began with surface vessels, helicopters and divers. The IMO casualty database (GISIS ref C0009519) logs a 'very serious marine casualty – capsizing/listing' at Escravos Oil Field, 5°26.80'N 4°57.50'E, 11 lives lost. The listed ship is the Liberian-flag tanker ALEKSEY KOSYGIN (IMO 9316127), with JASCON 4 (St Vincent & Grenadines flag) as the other ship involved.

DCN's dive support vessel Lewek Toucan (chartered by West African Ventures) was 17 hours' sailing away, doing saturation work on the Okpoho–Okono 16 pipeline project. The work stopped and the ship headed for the wreck. Its divers were in saturation at 70 m and were brought to 30 m saturation pressure during the 17-hour transit (DCN press release). AP quotes DCN's Tony Walker as saying the team was on a neighbouring oil field 120 km away.

Okene's own accounts: he forced the toilet door open in pitch darkness and saw three crewmates ahead of him swept away. He was then swept along a passageway into another toilet next to an officer's cabin, where he stayed about a day holding the overturned washbasin. He then swam into the officer's cabin and pulled off wall panelling to get out of the water. AP/The Nation add that he built a rack on a platform with two mattresses and found tools and a life vest with two flashlights. The flashlights died in under a day.
A Reuters report (Abuja, 28 May) quoted a West African Ventures spokeswoman: 'Unfortunately all twelve crew members are still missing.' Relatives had already been told there were no survivors.

Saturation divers deployed by diving bell were recovering bodies. Walker told AP they had already recovered four. Okene heard a boat, an anchor and hammering, and banged on the hull himself. He saw a diver's light, missed him once, and on the diver's return touched or grabbed him. The diver who found him was the South African Nicolaas (Nico) van Heerden, per BBC Outlook 2023. On the surface, project manager Tony Walker watched the helmet-camera feed in the control room. Global News gives 'the afternoon of May 28'.

Okene told Reuters he 'reached the surface at 19:32', more than 60 hours after the sinking. Before that, divers warmed him with hot water, gave him drinking water and an oxygen mask, and fitted a diving helmet/harness (suit) before leading him through the wreck to the pressurised bell. 04:50 on 26 May to 19:32 on 28 May is 62 h 42 min, which matches DCN's '62 hours trapped in the air pocket'. Here 'surface' means the bell and deck chamber, still under pressure.

Decompression in the deck chamber of the dive support vessel. Reported durations conflict. Okene to Reuters and AP: 60 hours. Jed Chamberlain (DCN Global) to BBC: two and a half days. DP officer Paul McDonald: 2 days. Chamberlain to The National: 'two to three days'. BBC Mundo 2023: three days (DISPUTED; best figure about 60 h, about 2.5 days). Sea Trucks' 31 May statement already says he 'has been brought to the surface safely', which fits about 60 h. BBC 2023: he was then flown by helicopter to hospital and sent home.

West African Ventures update: divers 'found and identified one survivor, Mr. Okene Harrison', the vessel's Nigerian cook, 'in a stable condition and under treatment on board the diving support vessel.' GM Jan Messchendorp thanked the divers.

Sea Trucks Group/WAV: the search and rescue operation was stopped for safety because the upside-down wreck at about 30 m had become too unstable for divers. Ten bodies were recovered, one crew member remained missing, and there was one survivor. CEO Jacques Roomans said the families had been informed.

Okene gave an exclusive interview to Nigeria's The Nation (Lagos) and attended a thanksgiving service at his Redeemed Christian Church of God parish. The Itsekiri Leaders of Thought called on NIMASA to investigate, asked for autopsies, and demanded compensation for the families.

DCN press release: 6 divers plus deck and technical crew; '1 person rescued alive, and 10 crew members retrieved from the wreck'; 'After 62 hours trapped in the air pocket, he was brought to the surface safe and well'.
Reuters interview published, conducted in Okene's home town of Warri. Photo credit Reuters/Joe Brock. Includes most of his best-documented quotes.
The National (Abu Dhabi) interviews Jed Chamberlain of DCN Global (UAE-based arm): 'They thought they were just looking for bodies.'
DCN Diving released the full helmet-camera video, shared with AP and AFP, and it went viral. AP confirmed its authenticity with DCN staff in the Netherlands.

AP interview at Okene's two-bedroom flat in Warri, his first with international media in person. He now works as a cook on land, vows never to return to the sea, has nightmares, did not attend the funerals, and was asked by his pastor whether he had used black magic.

Okene qualified as a commercial diver after a sponsored course at a commercial dive school in Gordon's Bay, South Africa (reported as Jacks Dive Chest; 'Class 3', placed 4th of 17). Rescue diver Nico van Heerden is reported to have presented his diploma. The primary Netwerk24/District Mail article is paywalled and was not read directly.
Australia's 9News interviewed Okene (only seen as quoted by LADbible). He is described as an IMCA Class 2 commercial air diver and is quoted: 'I'm enjoying diving, it's life for me, it's fun.'
BBC World Service Outlook ('Lost and Found: Trapped on the seabed', presenter India Rakusen) interviews Okene and diver Nicolaas van Heerden. A BBC Mundo article based on it ran on 17–18 Sep 2023.

No new verified interview or news about Okene was found. 2024 items such as LADbible are rewrites. Do not claim anything about his current status beyond 'reported in 2022–23 to be working as a commercial diver'.

key_facts.fact: Survivor: Harrison Odjegba Okene, Nigerian, 29 in 2013, the ship's cook, from Warri, Delta State. Company statements reversed his name as 'Mr. Okene Harrison'. His wife is Akpovona Okene (27 in Dec 2013).

Vessel: Jascon 4, an anchor-handling tug (AHT) owned and operated by West African Ventures Ltd (a Sea Trucks Group company) and working for Chevron Nigeria Ltd (operator of the NNPC/CNL joint venture). It was one of three tugs holding a tanker in 'tension/static tow' at SBM #3. The IMO casualty record gives the tanker as ALEKSEY KOSYGIN (Liberia) and Jascon 4's flag as St Vincent & Grenadines. VesselFinder gives IMO 9316256, built 2004 (aggregator only).

Location: off Escravos, Delta State, Niger Delta, Gulf of Guinea (Atlantic). Distance offshore is given as 15 nautical miles (owner), about 30 km (Chevron, DCN), 20 miles (Reuters) or 32 km (BBC). These are all consistent. An Itsekiri group's '30 nautical miles' is an outlier. IMO position: 5°26.80'N 4°57.50'E.
Depth: the wreck lay upside down at about 30 m. Owner and DCN give 30 m; AP gives about 100 ft; ABC quotes the owner as 98 ft. At 30 m the absolute pressure is about 4 atmospheres.

Weather/cause: Chevron's initial statement blamed 'heavy ocean swells'. BBC 2023 says 'bad weather'. Popular retellings add a 'rogue wave' or 'snapped tow rope', which are not established. A local group said Chevron and Seatrucks were 'trading blames'. No published final investigation finding was found.

Crew: 12 aboard. 11 died: 10 bodies recovered and 1 never found. Okene was the only survivor. AP, citing The Nation, says the dead were a Ukrainian captain and 10 Nigerians, including four young cadets from Nigeria's Maritime Academy. BBC Mundo 2023's '13 crew' is an outlier (DISPUTED). The names of the deceased were not found in any reliable published source and should not be used.

Hours trapped: DCN says 62 hours. Reuters/Okene: 'more than 60 hours', surfacing at 19:32 on 28 May; from 04:50 on 26 May that is about 62 h 42 min. AP headlines say '72 hours/three days', which is rounding up and should not be used (DISPUTED; use 'about 60 hours' or '62 hours').

Air pocket location: Reuters (from Okene) says the toilet next to an officer's cabin plus that cabin's bedroom, after he was swept there from the toilet he had been using. The Nation via Live Science says 'engineers' office'. Global News says a bathroom at the front of the vessel. BBC News published a diagram in 2023. The variant descriptions are DISPUTED; 'a small toilet and the officer's cabin next to it' is safest.

Air pocket size: Reuters says 'four foot high' (about 1.2 m) and calls the toilet 'four foot square'. Water was waist-deep (BBC 2023) and rising slowly. No measured volume exists. LLNL physicist Maxim Umansky estimated he needed about 25 m³ of surface-equivalent air for 60 h, or about 6 m³ when compressed about 4x at 30 m (roughly 6 x 10 x 3 ft). He speculated that the pocket was probably connected to a larger air space under the hull. These are estimates, not measurements.

What he did: he forced the toilet door open in darkness, then spent about a day holding the overturned washbasin to keep his head above water. He swam into the officer's cabin, pulled off wall panelling to make a platform, and piled two mattresses on a rack. He found tools and a life vest with two flashlights, which failed within a day. To be heard he hammered the hull. To Reuters he described using a water filter pulled from a water dispenser; to The Nation via AP, stripping the wall to bare steel and using a hammer. He wore only underpants or boxer shorts.

Coca-Cola: DISPUTED. AP (citing The Nation), The National and NBC TODAY say he survived on one bottle of Coke. Reuters, reporting after interviewing him, says he 'had nothing to eat or drink throughout his ordeal'. BBC Mundo 2023 says 'sin comida ni bebida' (no food or drink). Do not state it as fact; if mentioned, say 'some reports say'.

Sounds of fish: this is Okene's perception. To Reuters he said 'The fish came in and began eating the bodies. I could hear the sound.' AP says he heard fish, 'shark or barracudas he supposed'. BBC 2023 says he felt fish nibbling his own wounded skin. The species was never confirmed, so do not say 'sharks' as fact.

Water temperature: never measured or reported. 'Freezing cold water' (Reuters lead) and 'the temperature dropped to freezing' (AP) are figurative; this is tropical Gulf of Guinea water. His own words: 'I was very, very cold.' Do not put a number on screen.

Rescuers: a saturation-diving team from DCN Diving (Dutch, HQ Bergen op Zoom) and DCN Global (UAE arm), working from the West African Ventures-chartered dive support vessel Lewek Toucan. Six divers took part (DCN). Reuters says two South African divers rescued him; BBC 2023 says three divers went into the wreck. The diver who found him was South African Nicolaas 'Nico' van Heerden. Other named people: Tony Walker (project manager, watching in the control room), Jed Chamberlain (commercial manager, DCN Global), Paul McDonald (DP officer) and Alex Gibbs (life-support technician, 2022 account).

Mission: body recovery. Walker said the divers 'were looking only for bodies' and had already recovered four. Chamberlain: 'Amazingly, the recovery mission turned into a rescue mission.' Nuance: DCN's press release says that during transit 'the realisation grew among the divers that there could still be survivors… trapped in an air pocket.'

Words audible in DCN's helmet-cam footage, as transcribed by news outlets (quote cards only, not audio): diver 'He's alive! He's alive!' (TODAY/NBC, Global News); AP's version 'What's that? He's alive! He's alive!'; surface colleague 'Just reassure him. Just reassure him. Pat him on the shoulder.' (TODAY/NBC). Before the ascent, per AP, a voice asks for a thumbs-up and says 'Good job, my friend. Well done. You are a survivor.' The line 'corpse, corpse, a corpse' is Okene's recollection to AP, not a verified transcript.

Verified Okene quotes for quote cards, Reuters, Warri, published 12 Jun 2013: 'I was there in the water in total darkness just thinking it's the end. I kept thinking the water was going to fill up the room but it did not.' / 'I was very, very cold and it was black. I couldn't see anything.' / 'I was so hungry but mostly so, so thirsty. The salt water took the skin off my tongue.' / 'I heard a sound of a hammer hitting the vessel. Boom, boom, boom.' / 'I went into the water and tapped him. I was waving my hands and he was shocked.' / 'When I am at home sometimes it feels like the bed I am sleeping in is sinking. I think I'm still in the sea again. I jump up and I scream.' / 'I don't know what stopped the water from filling that room. I was calling on God. He did it. It was a miracle.'

Verified Okene quotes, AP interview in Warri, 5 Dec 2013: 'He came in but he was too fast, so I saw the light but before I could get to him, he was already out. I tried to follow him in the pitch darkness but I couldn't trace him, so I went back.' / 'So I tapped him at the back of his neck, so he was afraid.' / 'When he brought his hand close to me, I pulled on his hand.' / 'I knew when he gave me water he was observing me (to see) if I'm really human, because he was afraid.' / 'Every week I ask (God) 'Why only me? Why did my colleagues have to die?'' / 'When I was under the water I told God: If you rescue me, I will never go back to the sea again, never.' From The Nation, via AP: 'I was dazed and everywhere was dark as I was thrown from one end of the small cubicle to another.'

Rescuer and company quotes. Tony Walker (DCN), AP phone interview, 3 Dec 2013: 'The diver acknowledged that he had seen the hand and then, when he went to grab the hand, the hand grabbed him!' / 'It was frightening for everybody.' / 'He was incredibly lucky he was in an air pocket but he would have had a limited time (before) ... he wouldn't be able to breathe anymore.' Jed Chamberlain to The National, 12 Jun 2013: 'It was incredible. They thought they were just looking for bodies.' Paul McDonald (DPO), gCaptain, May 2013: 'All on board could not believe how cool he was when being rescued.' DCN, 10 Jun 2013: 'After 62 hours trapped in the air pocket, he was brought to the surface safe and well'.

Recovery procedure: after more than 60 h at about 4 atm his tissues were saturated with nitrogen, so a direct ascent risked fatal decompression sickness. The divers warmed him with hot water, gave him water and an oxygen mask, and fitted a helmet and harness. They led him through the silted wreck to the pressurised diving bell, which mated to the deck decompression chamber. He then spent about 60 h, or about 2.5 days, decompressing (reported 2 to 3 days; DISPUTED range). Chamberlain told the BBC the divers had to teach him to use the gear and that he was 'absolutely calm'.

Injuries and condition: skin peeling after days in salt water; seawater 'took the skin off my tongue'; thirst and hunger; bruises from being thrown about (BBC 2023). The owner described him as 'in a stable condition' after a medical check. After the chamber he was flown by helicopter to hospital and released home (BBC 2023). Ongoing nightmares and survivor's guilt.

facts.aftermath:
Investigations: West African Ventures said in May 2013 that it had 'commenced a full investigation'. Chevron gave 'heavy ocean swells' as the initial cause. In June 2013 the Itsekiri Leaders of Thought (Warri) asked NIMASA to investigate, requested autopsies of the 11 crew, demanded adequate compensation for the families, and criticised Chevron and Seatrucks for 'trading blames'. The IMO GISIS database records the casualty (ref C0009519): very serious marine casualty, capsizing, 11 lives lost, listed under the tanker ALEKSEY KOSYGIN (Liberia), with Jascon 4 as the other ship. It appears in an IMO III Sub-Committee lessons-learned list (2020 session). No published final cause finding and no public figure for compensation to families were found. Do not claim either. The wreck search was abandoned on 31 May 2013 because the hull was unstable, and one crew member was never recovered.

Okene, 2013: he gave thanks at his Redeemed Christian Church of God parish. He told Reuters (June 2013) that he had nightmares, that his bed felt as if it were sinking, and that he was unsure he would return to the sea. In December 2013, after DCN released the helmet-cam video (2–4 Dec) and it went viral, he told AP in Warri that he had taken a job as a cook on land, vowed 'never' to go back to sea, skipped colleagues' funerals for fear of families' reactions, and had been asked by his own pastor whether he used black magic. His wife Akpovona described his night terrors.

Later life (reported, partly secondary): in 2015 he trained as a commercial diver in South Africa. A Gordon's Bay commercial dive school (reported as Jacks Dive Chest) sponsored him; he was reported as 'Class 3' qualified and placed 4th of 17 (Netwerk24/District Mail, 8 Jul 2015; paywalled, not read directly). The rescue diver Nico van Heerden is reported to have presented his diploma (ExplorersWeb). A 2022 9News interview, quoted by LADbible in 2023, describes him as an IMCA Class 2 commercial air diver: 'I'm enjoying diving, it's life for me, it's fun.' In BBC World Service Outlook (30 Aug 2023), with van Heerden, he said a later car accident pushed him toward professional diving: his car went off a bridge into a lake, he escaped and saved a companion. This detail is single-sourced via BBC Mundo. BBC Mundo also quotes him (in Spanish translation) as saying he stays near the ocean because it is 'his environment'. He became an air diver, not a saturation diver. Nothing newer than 2023–24 was found as of Nov 2026. State his current status only as 'reported in 2022–23 to work as a commercial diver'.
myths: '72 hours / three full days underwater': that is AP's rounding. DCN says 62 hours, and Okene's own timing (04:50 on 26 May to 19:32 on 28 May) is about 62–63 h.
'He survived by drinking Coca-Cola': disputed. AP, The National and TODAY say one bottle of Coke; Reuters and BBC 2023 say he had nothing to eat or drink.
'Freezing water': figurative. No temperature was recorded; the Gulf of Guinea is tropical. He said he was 'very, very cold', and long immersion still risked hypothermia.
'Sharks ate his crewmates': he heard, and later said he felt, fish. He 'supposed' sharks or barracuda, but the species was never confirmed.
'He was at the bottom of the deep Atlantic': the wreck lay at about 30 m in coastal shelf water about 30 km offshore.
'The divers were on a rescue mission': it was a body-recovery dive. Four bodies had already been recovered when he was found. DCN does say the divers had begun to hope for survivors.
'It was a fishing boat' (ExplorersWeb): wrong. It was an anchor-handling tug holding a tanker at a Chevron loading buoy.
'Dutch divers' vs 'South African divers': both are true. The company was Dutch (DCN Diving, with its UAE arm DCN Global) and the divers were South African.
'It happened in December 2013': the video was released in December 2013; the capsize was on 26 May 2013.
'13 crew' (BBC Mundo 2023): every 2013 source says 12 aboard, 11 dead.
'A rogue wave smashed it' / 'tow rope snapped': these are embellishments. Chevron cited heavy ocean swells, and no published final cause was found.
'He was brought straight up / walked out on deck': he was moved under pressure in a diving bell to a deck chamber and decompressed for about 60 h (reports range from 2 to 3 days).
'The tug capsized but did not sink' (early gCaptain update): it sank and lay upside down on the seabed.
'He found the air pocket in the toilet he was using': he was swept along a passageway into a different toilet next to an officer's cabin.
'The other crew died because doors were locked against pirates': this is AP's paraphrase of Okene's assumption ('they would have locked themselves into their cabins'), not an established finding.
'He became a saturation diver': he qualified as a commercial air diver (Class 3 in 2015, later reportedly IMCA Class 2).

Quotes circulating without a traceable source, which should not be used: 'It was around 5 am and I was on the toilet when the vessel just started going down…', 'I was crying and calling on Jesus to rescue me…' (ExplorersWeb, origin unknown), and 'I have faced a lot of my fears in my life…' (attributed by Soundings to 'The Guardian'; could not be located).
facts.sensitivities:
Eleven men died: by AP's account (citing The Nation), a Ukrainian captain and 10 Nigerians, including four young Maritime Academy cadets. One was never recovered. Their names do not appear in reliable published sources; do not name or invent them, and do not depict their deaths, bodies or faces. Avoid visualising Okene's 'three guys washed away' moment or the fish feeding on bodies. If needed, convey it only through his own attributed words, or leave it out. Okene's own pain should not be sensationalised: survivor's guilt ('Why only me?'), not attending the funerals, nightmares, and his pastor asking whether he used black magic. The black-magic angle is stigmatising and is best omitted or handled in one neutral line. His Christian faith is central to his own telling, so quote it accurately without proselytising.

No blame: no published investigation found fault. Do not imply negligence by Chevron, West African Ventures/Sea Trucks or the crew. Present 'locked cabins because of pirates' only as AP's report of his assumption, or omit it.

Copyright and likeness: do not use DCN's helmet-cam video or audio, AP/Reuters photos, or BBC audio. Use on-screen quote cards with attribution (speaker, outlet, date). Draw Okene and the divers as non-photographic, non-identifying figures such as silhouettes or a hand reaching from dark water. Do not make a realistic portrait of him. Video dialogue ('He's alive! He's alive!', 'Just reassure him…') should be attributed as 'as heard in DCN Diving helmet-camera footage, transcribed by AP/NBC'. BBC Outlook 2023 quotes are available here only in BBC Mundo's Spanish translation. If used, mark them as translated, or prefer the English Reuters and AP quotes.

Accuracy flags for narration: use 'about 60 hours' or '62 hours' (not 72) and '30 m' (not 'the bottom of the ocean'). Give decompression as about 60 hours / about 2.5 days ('reported 2–3 days'). Do not give a water-temperature number. Hedge or omit the Coke detail. Use 04:50 for the capsize time (AP's 04:30 conflicts). Okene is a living private person; keep claims about his present life to what was reported in 2022–23.

quotes.speaker: Harrison Okene
quotes.words_en: I was there in the water in total darkness just thinking it's the end. I kept thinking the water was going to fill up the room but it did not.
quotes.context: Reuters interview by Joe Brock in Warri, Nigeria, published 12 June 2013, about two weeks after the rescue. He is describing the air pocket.
quotes.korean: 저는 완전한 어둠 속 물 안에 있으면서 '이제 끝이구나' 하는 생각만 했어요. 물이 방을 가득 채울 거라고 계속 생각했는데, 그렇게 되지 않았어요.

quotes.speaker: Harrison Okene
quotes.words_en: I was so hungry but mostly so, so thirsty. The salt water took the skin off my tongue.
quotes.context: Reuters interview, Warri, 12 June 2013. Reuters adds that he had nothing to eat or drink, which conflicts with other accounts of a bottle of Coke (see notes).
quotes.korean: 너무 배가 고팠지만, 무엇보다 정말, 정말 목이 말랐어요. 바닷물 때문에 혀 껍질이 벗겨졌어요.

quotes.speaker: Harrison Okene
quotes.words_en: As I was coming out of the toilet it was pitch black so we were trying to link our way out to the water tidal (exit hatch)
quotes.context: Reuters, Warri, 12 June 2013, about the first minutes after the capsize at about 04:50 on 26 May 2013. 'water tidal (exit hatch)' is Reuters' own transcription and bracket. He almost certainly means 'watertight [door]', which is what he says in the 2024 testimony.
quotes.korean: 화장실에서 나올 때 칠흑같이 어두워서, 우리는 수밀문(탈출 해치) 쪽으로 더듬어 빠져나가려 하고 있었어요.

quotes.speaker: Harrison Okene
quotes.words_en: Three guys were in front of me and suddenly water rushed in full force. I saw the first one, the second one, the third one just washed away. I knew these guys were dead.
quotes.context: Reuters, Warri, 12 June 2013, describing the passage to the exit hatch. SENSITIVE: these are deaths of named crew. Use only as text, without dramatising or illustrating the bodies.
quotes.korean: 제 앞에 세 사람이 있었는데, 갑자기 물이 엄청난 힘으로 밀려들었어요. 첫 번째, 두 번째, 세 번째 사람이 그냥 휩쓸려 가는 걸 봤어요. 그들이 죽었다는 걸 알았어요.

quotes.speaker: Harrison Okene
quotes.words_en: I was very, very cold and it was black. I couldn't see anything.
quotes.context: Reuters, Warri, 12 June 2013, about the officer's cabin where he built a small raft from wall panelling.
quotes.korean: 정말, 정말 추웠고, 캄캄했어요. 아무것도 보이지 않았어요.

quotes.speaker: Harrison Okene
quotes.words_en: But I could perceive the dead bodies of my crew were nearby. I could smell them. The fish came in and began eating the bodies. I could hear the sound. It was horror.
quotes.context: Reuters, Warri, 12 June 2013. RECOMMEND NOT USING the bodies and fish lines out of respect for the families. 'It was horror' could be used alone if needed.
quotes.korean: 하지만 동료 선원들의 시신이 근처에 있다는 걸 느낄 수 있었어요. 냄새가 났어요. 물고기들이 들어와 시신을 먹기 시작했어요. 그 소리가 들렸어요. 공포 그 자체였어요.

quotes.speaker: Harrison Okene
quotes.words_en: I heard a sound of a hammer hitting the vessel. Boom, boom, boom. I swam down and found a water dispenser. I pulled the water filter and I hammered the side of the vessel hoping someone would hear me. Then the diver must have heard a sound.
quotes.context: Reuters, Warri, 12 June 2013, about the afternoon of 28 May 2013 when the divers arrived.
quotes.korean: 망치로 배를 두드리는 소리가 들렸어요. 쿵, 쿵, 쿵. 아래로 헤엄쳐 내려가 정수기를 찾았어요. 정수 필터를 뽑아서, 누군가 듣기를 바라며 배 옆면을 두드렸어요. 그러자 잠수부가 그 소리를 들었던 게 분명해요.

quotes.speaker: Harrison Okene
quotes.words_en: I went into the water and tapped him. I was waving my hands and he was shocked.
quotes.context: Reuters, Warri, 12 June 2013, about the moment he reached the diver's head-torch light.
quotes.korean: 물속으로 들어가 그를 툭 쳤어요. 제가 손을 흔들자 그는 깜짝 놀랐어요.

quotes.speaker: Harrison Okene
quotes.words_en: When I am at home sometimes it feels like the bed I am sleeping in is sinking. I think I'm still in the sea again. I jump up and I scream.
quotes.context: Reuters, Warri, 12 June 2013, about the aftermath and trauma.
quotes.korean: 집에 있으면 가끔 제가 자는 침대가 가라앉는 것처럼 느껴져요. 아직도 바닷속에 있는 것 같아요. 벌떡 일어나 비명을 질러요.

quotes.speaker: Harrison Okene
quotes.words_en: I don't know what stopped the water from filling that room. I was calling on God. He did it. It was a miracle.
quotes.context: Reuters, Warri, 12 June 2013. This is the closing quote of the Reuters story.
quotes.korean: 무엇이 물이 그 방을 채우지 못하게 막았는지 모르겠어요. 저는 하나님을 부르고 있었어요. 그분이 하신 거예요. 기적이었어요.

quotes.speaker: Harrison Okene
quotes.words_en: I was dazed and everywhere was dark as I was thrown from one end of the small cubicle to another.
quotes.context: Exclusive interview with Nigeria's The Nation newspaper, June 2013, about the moment of capsize while he was in the toilet. The Nation original was not retrievable, so this is quoted via the AP (3 Dec 2013) and The Telegraph (12 Jun 2013).
reported_by: AP via Post and Courier / Press Herald / CBC (3 Dec 2013)
The Telegraph (12 Jun 2013), reprinted at kiyoandfilo.blogspot.com
quotes.korean: 작은 칸 안에서 이쪽 끝에서 저쪽 끝으로 내동댕이쳐지는 동안, 정신은 멍했고 사방이 캄캄했어요.

quotes.speaker: Harrison Okene
quotes.words_en: I made my way out of the toilet, groped through the dark into a place I imagined was the officers' rest room. From there I moved to engineers' office. I wasn't seeing, I was just feeling my way with my hands.
quotes.context: The Nation interview, June 2013, as reprinted by The Telegraph on 12 June 2013. Fox News gives it slightly differently: 'officers' restroom ... I wasn't seeing [anything]'.
quotes.korean: 화장실에서 빠져나와, 어둠 속을 더듬으며 사관 휴게실이라고 짐작한 곳으로 갔어요. 거기서 기관사 사무실로 옮겨 갔어요. 보이지 않았어요. 그냥 손으로 더듬으며 길을 찾았어요.

quotes.speaker: Harrison Okene
quotes.words_en: I started calling on the name of God. ... I started reminiscing on the verses I read before I slept. I read the Bible from Psalm 54 to 92. My wife had sent me the verses to read that night when she called me before I went to bed.
quotes.context: The Nation interview, June 2013, quoted by AP on 3 Dec 2013. He is praying in the air pocket.
reported_by: AP via CBC / Post and Courier / Irish Times / The National (UAE)
quotes.korean: 하나님의 이름을 부르기 시작했어요. … 자기 전에 읽었던 말씀을 되새기기 시작했어요. 저는 시편 54편부터 92편까지 읽었어요. 그날 밤 자기 전에 아내가 전화해서, 읽으라고 그 구절들을 보내 줬거든요.

quotes.speaker: Harrison Okene
quotes.words_en: I prayed about a hundred times. When I was tired, I started calling on the name of God. I was just calling on His name for divine intervention.
quotes.context: The Telegraph, 12 June 2013. Most of it is attributed to The Nation interview, but the Telegraph does not say who recorded 'I prayed about a hundred times'.
quotes.korean: 백 번쯤 기도했어요. 지치면 하나님의 이름을 부르기 시작했어요. 그저 하나님이 개입해 주시길 바라며 그분의 이름을 불렀어요.

quotes.speaker: Harrison Okene
quotes.words_en: At that point I was very scared. I said: 'So this is how I am going to die?' What would happen to my wife? So she will become a widow? I don't even have a child yet. What about my mother and everybody I love – so I will never see them again?
quotes.context: The Nation interview, June 2013, via The Telegraph (12 Jun 2013). It follows the sounds of fish in the wreck. Soundings quotes a shorter version.
quotes.korean: 그 순간 너무 무서웠어요. 저는 말했어요. '내가 이렇게 죽는 건가?' 아내는 어떻게 되지? 과부가 되는 건가? 난 아직 아이도 없는데. 어머니와 내가 사랑하는 모든 사람은? 다시는 그들을 못 보는 건가?

quotes.speaker: Harrison Okene
quotes.words_en: Then I heard a sound like anchor dropping again. I also heard sound of paddling and divers' craft moving around the boat. I heard a hammering sound from afar.
quotes.context: The Nation interview, June 2013, via The Telegraph, about the divers arriving on 28 May.
quotes.korean: 그러다 또 닻을 내리는 것 같은 소리가 들렸어요. 노 젓는 소리와 잠수부들의 배가 보트 주위를 오가는 소리도 들렸어요. 멀리서 망치질 소리가 들렸어요.

quotes.speaker: Harrison Okene
quotes.words_en: I started using the hammer to hit the wall to attract the divers. I heard them moving about. They were far away from where I was. I did that for some minutes and stopped. After a while, the sound died.
quotes.context: The Nation, June 2013, via The Telegraph. AP's version of the same quote reads: 'I heard them moving away. They were far away from where I was.' The two disagree on 'moving about' versus 'moving away'.
reported_by: AP via CBC / Irish Times / The National
quotes.korean: 잠수부들의 주의를 끌려고 망치로 벽을 치기 시작했어요. 그들이 움직이는 소리가 들렸어요. 그들은 제가 있는 곳에서 멀리 있었어요. 몇 분 동안 그렇게 하다가 멈췄어요. 얼마 뒤 소리가 사라졌어요.

quotes.speaker: Harrison Okene
quotes.words_en: I touched his head and he was shocked. He was searching and I just saw the light, so I jumped into the water. As he was shocked, he stretched out his hands.
quotes.context: The Nation, June 2013, via The Telegraph. Soundings and Fox add: 'When I located him, I was the one who touched the diver ... I touched him.' and 'My hands and feet were very white [pale].'
quotes.korean: 제가 그의 머리를 만졌고 그는 깜짝 놀랐어요. 그는 수색 중이었고, 저는 불빛을 보자마자 물속으로 뛰어들었어요. 그가 놀라면서 손을 뻗었어요.

quotes.speaker: Harrison Okene (recalling the voice on the diver's speaker)
quotes.words_en: There is a survivor, he is alive.
quotes.context: What Okene says he heard from the diver's speaker. The Nation (June 2013, via the Telegraph) gives it as above. AP (3 Dec 2013) gives 'There's a survivor! He's alive.' AP (11 Dec 2013) gives 'He's alive! He's alive! He's alive!' This is his memory of the moment, not a transcript.
reported_by: AP via CBC / Press Herald (3 Dec 2013)
quotes.korean: 생존자가 있다, 살아 있다.

quotes.speaker: Harrison Okene
quotes.words_en: At that point I knew there was nothing I could do for myself. I just had to wait and see.
quotes.context: The Nation, June 2013, via The Telegraph. In the article it comes after the divers put a helmet and harness on him, but the exact moment it refers to is unclear.
quotes.korean: 그 순간 제 스스로 할 수 있는 게 아무것도 없다는 걸 알았어요. 그저 기다리며 지켜볼 수밖에 없었어요.

quotes.speaker: Harrison Okene
quotes.words_en: When we came out, I saw the stars in the sky and I thought I must have been in the water for the whole day. I thought it was the Sunday evening. It was after I left that I was told that I had spent over two days there.
quotes.context: The Nation, June 2013, via The Telegraph. LiveScience quotes the last sentence as 'after I left the DCC [decompression chamber]'. The Telegraph says that on arriving at the surface at about 7pm on Tuesday 28 May he thought he had been trapped for only 12 hours. When he 'came out' is unclear (see notes).
quotes.korean: 밖으로 나왔을 때 하늘에 별이 보였고, 저는 물속에 하루 종일 있었던 거라고 생각했어요. 일요일 저녁인 줄 알았어요. 나온 뒤에야 거기서 이틀 넘게 있었다는 말을 들었어요.

quotes.speaker: Harrison Okene
quotes.words_en: It was around 5am and I was on the toilet when the vessel just started going down – the speed was so, so fast.
quotes.context: Phone interview from Warri, published in The Guardian (UK) around 13 June 2013 and reprinted in the Taipei Times on 14 June 2013.
reported_by: Taipei Times reprint of The Guardian (14 Jun 2013)
quotes.korean: 새벽 5시쯤이었고 저는 화장실에 있었는데, 배가 그냥 가라앉기 시작했어요. 속도가 정말, 정말 빨랐어요.

quotes.speaker: Harrison Okene
quotes.words_en: All around me was just black, and noisy. I was crying and calling on Jesus to rescue me, I prayed so hard. I was so hungry and thirsty and cold and I was just praying to see some kind of light.
quotes.context: The Guardian (UK), around 13 June 2013, by phone from Warri, about his time in the air pocket.
reported_by: Taipei Times reprint of The Guardian
quotes.korean: 제 주변은 온통 캄캄했고, 시끄러웠어요. 저는 울면서 예수님께 구해 달라고 부르짖었어요. 정말 간절히 기도했어요. 너무 배고프고 목마르고 추웠고, 그저 어떤 빛이라도 보게 해 달라고 기도하고 있었어요.

quotes.speaker: Harrison Okene
quotes.words_en: I went to the water and touched the diver. He himself shivered from fear. So I stepped back and just held my hand in the waters and waved it in front of his camera so they would see the images above deck.
quotes.context: The Guardian (UK), around 13 June 2013, about the moment the diver's light came near.
reported_by: Taipei Times reprint of The Guardian
quotes.korean: 물속으로 들어가 잠수부를 만졌어요. 그 사람도 두려움에 몸을 떨었어요. 그래서 저는 뒤로 물러나 물속에서 손을 내밀고, 갑판 위에서 영상을 볼 수 있도록 그의 카메라 앞에서 흔들었어요.

quotes.speaker: Harrison Okene
quotes.words_en: They told me all the others had died and I cried, because I thought I was the only one who had been trapped in the boat
quotes.context: The Guardian (UK), around 13 June 2013, about learning after the rescue that he was the sole survivor. Only one source: the Taipei Times reprint, read through a fetch tool. His 2024 testimony describes the same moment, in the diving bell.
reported_by: Taipei Times reprint of The Guardian (14 Jun 2013)
quotes.korean: 다른 사람들은 모두 죽었다고 들었을 때 저는 울었어요. 배 안에 갇힌 사람은 저 하나뿐이라고 생각했거든요.

quotes.speaker: Harrison Okene
quotes.words_en: I heard people shouting, I felt the vessel going down, going down, I heard a voice saying 'Is this vessel sinking or what?' ... I was in the WC (toilet) and the WC fell on my head, things started falling on my head ... My colleagues were shouting 'God help me, God help me, God help me.' Then after a while I never heard from them (again).
quotes.context: AP interview by Sunday Alamba at his flat in Warri on 5 Dec 2013, published 11 Dec 2013 (his first international interview). SENSITIVE: these are the last words of his colleagues. Use with great restraint or not at all.
quotes.korean: 사람들이 소리치는 게 들렸고, 배가 가라앉고, 또 가라앉는 게 느껴졌어요. '이 배 가라앉는 거야, 뭐야?' 하는 목소리가 들렸어요… 저는 화장실에 있었는데 변기가 머리 위로 떨어졌고, 물건들이 머리 위로 떨어지기 시작했어요… 동료들이 '하나님 살려 주세요, 하나님 살려 주세요, 하나님 살려 주세요' 하고 외치고 있었어요. 그러다 얼마 뒤로는 그들의 소리를 (다시는) 듣지 못했어요.

quotes.speaker: Harrison Okene
quotes.words_en: He came in but he was too fast, so I saw the light but before I could get to him, he was already out. I tried to follow him in the pitch darkness but I couldn't trace him, so I went back.
quotes.context: AP, Warri, 5 Dec 2013 (published 11 Dec), about the first diver passing. DCN's Jed Chamberlain told the BBC he missed the first diver's hand and caught the second one.
quotes.korean: 그가 들어왔는데 너무 빨랐어요. 불빛은 봤지만 제가 다가가기도 전에 그는 이미 나가 버렸어요. 칠흑 같은 어둠 속에서 따라가 보려 했지만 찾을 수 없어서 돌아왔어요.

quotes.speaker: Harrison Okene
quotes.words_en: So I tapped him at the back of his neck, so he was afraid.
quotes.context: AP, Warri, 5 Dec 2013, when the diver returned. Other accounts differ: 'I touched his head' (The Nation) and 'tapped him' (Reuters).
quotes.korean: 그래서 그의 목 뒤를 툭 쳤어요. 그러자 그가 겁을 먹었어요.

quotes.speaker: Diver (as recalled by Okene to AP)
quotes.words_en: corpse, corpse, a corpse
quotes.context: AP (11 Dec 2013) reports this as what the diver said into his microphone on seeing the hand, based on Okene's recollection. It is not audible in the published footage: the captions and AFP's transcript have the surface supervisor asking 'you found one, yeah?'. Do not present it as footage audio.
quotes.korean: 시신, 시신, 시신이다.

quotes.speaker: Harrison Okene
quotes.words_en: When he brought his hand close to me, I pulled on his hand.
quotes.context: AP, Warri, 5 Dec 2013 (published 11 Dec), the moment the diver realised he was alive.
quotes.korean: 그가 손을 제 쪽으로 가까이 가져왔을 때, 제가 그의 손을 잡아당겼어요.

quotes.speaker: Harrison Okene
quotes.words_en: I knew when he gave me water he was observing me (to see) if I'm really human, because he was afraid.
quotes.context: AP, Warri, 5 Dec 2013, about the diver handing him a bottle of water inside the air pocket.
quotes.korean: 그가 저에게 물을 줄 때, 제가 정말 사람인지 살펴보고 있다는 걸 알았어요. 그가 겁을 먹고 있었으니까요.

quotes.speaker: Harrison Okene
quotes.words_en: When I was under the water I told God: If you rescue me, I will never go back to the sea again, never.
quotes.context: AP, Warri, 5 Dec 2013, about the vow he made on the seabed. He later broke it and became a commercial diver in 2015.
quotes.korean: 물속에 있을 때 하나님께 말했어요. 저를 구해 주시면 다시는 바다로 돌아가지 않겠다고요. 절대로요.

quotes.speaker: Harrison Okene
quotes.words_en: Every week I ask (God) 'Why only me? Why did my colleagues have to die?'
quotes.context: AP, Warri, 5 Dec 2013, about survivor's guilt.
quotes.korean: 매주 (하나님께) 묻습니다. '왜 저만입니까? 왜 제 동료들은 죽어야 했습니까?'

quotes.speaker: Harrison Okene
quotes.words_en: I couldn't go because I didn't know what the family will say, thinking 'Why is he the only one to survive,'
quotes.context: AP, Warri, 5 Dec 2013, explaining why he did not attend his colleagues' funerals.
quotes.korean: 갈 수 없었어요. 유족들이 '왜 저 사람만 살아남았지' 하고 생각하며 무슨 말을 할지 몰랐으니까요.

quotes.speaker: Akpovona Okene (Harrison's wife, 27)
quotes.words_en: When he is sleeping, he has that shock, he will just wake up in the night saying 'Honey see, the bed is sinking, we are in the sea.'
quotes.context: AP, Warri, 5 Dec 2013 (published 11 Dec), about his nightmares.
quotes.korean: 남편은 자다가 그 충격이 와요. 한밤중에 갑자기 깨서 '여보, 봐, 침대가 가라앉고 있어, 우리 바다에 있어'라고 말해요.

quotes.speaker: Harrison Okene
quotes.words_en: I thought of my family, thought of my mom, my brothers, my wife. I have access to none of them. No way to get to them.
quotes.context: On camera in the AP video 'Man Rescued From Sunken Boat Talks About Ordeal' (YouTube xrO2ENzr2cM, 11 Dec 2013), filmed in Warri. Transcribed from YouTube auto-captions: check by ear before quoting on screen.
quotes.korean: 가족 생각을 했어요. 어머니, 형제들, 아내 생각을요. 그 누구에게도 닿을 수 없었어요. 그들에게 갈 방법이 없었어요.

quotes.speaker: Harrison Okene
quotes.words_en: I know I'm going to die but the only thing I could put my hope and trust in and my confidence in is God.
quotes.context: AP on-camera interview (YouTube xrO2ENzr2cM, 11 Dec 2013). Transcribed from auto-captions: check by ear.
quotes.korean: 제가 죽을 거라는 걸 알았어요. 하지만 제가 희망과 믿음과 확신을 둘 수 있는 유일한 존재는 하나님이었어요.

quotes.speaker: Harrison Okene
quotes.words_en: If death comes, let it come. If death did not come, I know he's going to rescue me. ... I kept calm and I was bold because I was not afraid anymore
quotes.context: AP on-camera interview (YouTube xrO2ENzr2cM, 11 Dec 2013). The captions read 'let it comes'. Transcribed from auto-captions: check by ear.
quotes.korean: 죽음이 온다면, 오라고 해라. 죽음이 오지 않는다면, 그분이 나를 구해 주실 걸 안다. … 저는 침착했고 담대했어요. 더 이상 두렵지 않았으니까요.

quotes.speaker: Harrison Okene
quotes.words_en: I don't know it's up to 3 days because I was thinking just a day, maybe it's getting into the evening.
quotes.context: AP on-camera interview (YouTube xrO2ENzr2cM, 11 Dec 2013), about losing track of time. Transcribed from auto-captions: check by ear.
reported_by: compare The Telegraph/The Nation: 'I thought it was the Sunday evening'
quotes.korean: 그게 3일이나 될 줄은 몰랐어요. 그냥 하루, 아마 저녁쯤 되어 가는 줄 알았거든요.

quotes.speaker: Psalm 54 (recited by Okene, per AP)
quotes.words_en: Oh God, by your name, save me. ... The Lord sustains my life.
quotes.context: AP (3 Dec 2013) says Okene recited the last psalm his wife had texted him, 'sometimes called the Prayer for Deliverance'. These are scripture words (Psalm 54:1 and 54:4) in AP's rendering, not Okene's own words.
reported_by: AP via CBC / Post and Courier / Irish Times / The National / TheJournal.ie
quotes.korean: 하나님이여, 주의 이름으로 나를 구원하소서… 주께서 내 생명을 붙드시나이다.

quotes.speaker: Harrison Okene
quotes.words_en: I tried to kill the fear in front of me. Because one thing that can kill you fast is fear. That panic that comes at you, it kills you before your real death comes. Because the moment you start panicking, you use too much oxygen.
quotes.context: The Guardian feature (Paula Cocozza), Aug/Sep 2023: 'I survived three days in a capsized boat on the ocean floor – praying in my air bubble'. The Guardian page could not be fetched, but three reprints give identical wording.
quotes.korean: 눈앞의 두려움을 죽이려고 애썼어요. 사람을 가장 빨리 죽일 수 있는 것 중 하나가 두려움이거든요. 밀려오는 공포는 진짜 죽음이 오기도 전에 사람을 죽여요. 당황하기 시작하는 순간 산소를 너무 많이 쓰게 되니까요.

quotes.speaker: Harrison Okene
quotes.words_en: instead of panicking, you have to think of a way out.
quotes.context: The Guardian 2023 feature, via reprints: what he told himself when trapped in the second toilet. Unilad gives 'But I told myself, instead of panicking, you have to think of a way out.'
reported_by: All That's Interesting (Apr 2025, citing The Guardian 2023)
quotes.korean: 당황하는 대신, 빠져나갈 방법을 생각해야 해.

quotes.speaker: Harrison Okene
quotes.words_en: The air couldn't go out of the boat completely. Some had to be trapped inside.
quotes.context: The Guardian 2023 feature, via reprints. He is explaining why an air pocket existed: the crew kept cabin doors shut against pirates.
quotes.korean: 공기가 배 밖으로 완전히 빠져나갈 수는 없었어요. 일부는 안에 갇혀 있을 수밖에 없었죠.

quotes.speaker: Harrison Okene
quotes.words_en: If you got stuck in any room, you were lost. It was totally dark, I was confused. If you don't act fast, you can lose your life there.
quotes.context: The Guardian 2023 feature, via reprint. Only one source (All That's Interesting).
quotes.korean: 어느 방에든 갇히면 끝이었어요. 완전히 캄캄했고, 저는 혼란스러웠어요. 빨리 움직이지 않으면 거기서 목숨을 잃을 수 있었어요.

quotes.speaker: Harrison Okene
quotes.words_en: I did not have the patience to wait.
quotes.context: The Guardian 2023 feature, via reprint, about leaving his crewmates at the exit hatch. Only one source.
quotes.korean: 기다릴 인내심이 없었어요.

quotes.speaker: Harrison Okene
quotes.words_en: Everything was normal. My temperature, blood pressure. I thought, that's not normal.
quotes.context: The Guardian 2023 feature, via reprints, about the medical checks in the decompression chamber after the rescue.
quotes.korean: 모든 게 정상이었어요. 체온도, 혈압도요. 저는 생각했죠. '이건 정상이 아닌데.'

quotes.speaker: Harrison Okene
quotes.words_en: I have faced a lot of my fears in my life, and I decided to face this once and for all. I know it should be my fear, but I don't need to be scared of water. Because I need to embrace my fear once and for all and be strong. Our happiness, our joy, our future – they are all in our hands. I had to reprogramme my thinking. I balanced my mind.
quotes.context: The Guardian 2023 feature, via reprints, about deciding in 2015 to train as a commercial diver.
reported_by: Soundings ('Life After Surviving Inside a Capsized, Sunken Tug')
quotes.korean: 저는 살면서 많은 두려움과 마주해 왔고, 이번 것도 완전히 끝내 버리기로 했어요. 그게 제 두려움이어야 한다는 건 알지만, 물을 무서워할 필요는 없어요. 두려움을 완전히 끌어안고 강해져야 하니까요. 우리의 행복, 기쁨, 미래는 모두 우리 손에 달려 있어요. 생각을 다시 프로그래밍해야 했어요. 마음의 균형을 잡았어요.

quotes.speaker: Harrison Okene
quotes.words_en: I was struggling to stay alive, wondering how long it (the air pocket) would last me. ... I was thinking about my family, my wife, what would happen, how would she live, how can I get out, thinking about my life as well.
quotes.context: Interview with Australia's 9News (2022), quoted by LADbible on 31 Aug 2023. The 9News original was not retrieved.
quotes.korean: 살아남으려고 몸부림치면서, 이 공기주머니가 얼마나 버텨 줄지 생각했어요. … 가족 생각, 아내 생각을 했어요. 어떻게 될까, 아내는 어떻게 살아갈까, 어떻게 나갈 수 있을까, 제 인생에 대해서도요.

quotes.speaker: Harrison Okene
quotes.words_en: Before we knew, we were sinking.
quotes.context: 9News (2022), via LADbible 31 Aug 2023, about the capsize.
quotes.korean: 미처 알아차리기도 전에, 우리는 가라앉고 있었어요.

quotes.speaker: Harrison Okene
quotes.words_en: I'm enjoying diving, it's life for me, it's fun.
quotes.context: 9News (2022), via LADbible 2023. He was by then an IMCA Class Two commercial air diver.
quotes.korean: 다이빙이 즐거워요. 저에게는 삶이고, 재미예요.

quotes.speaker: Harrison Okene
quotes.words_en: the place was dark like nothing; if someone can even pass me 10 times I will not recognize that somebody's passing by
quotes.context: His own testimony on the YouTube faith channel 'Stories of Faith' (Bukola Anney, video rkPT4j4CuXA, Feb 2024). Transcribed from auto-captions and lightly cleaned. This is a low-tier source: check by ear.
quotes.korean: 그곳은 아무것도 없는 것처럼 캄캄했어요. 누가 제 옆을 열 번 지나가도, 누가 지나가는 줄 알아채지 못했을 거예요.

quotes.speaker: Harrison Okene
quotes.words_en: at the early beginning I was panicking I was so afraid but it got to a stage I was no longer afraid
quotes.context: 'Stories of Faith' testimony (YouTube rkPT4j4CuXA, Feb 2024), from auto-captions. It matches the AP 2013 video ('I was not afraid anymore').
quotes.korean: 처음에는 공황 상태였고 정말 무서웠어요. 하지만 어느 순간부터는 더 이상 두렵지 않았어요.

quotes.speaker: Harrison Okene
quotes.words_en: I want people to know that I'm not afraid of my fear ... I believe someday inside of me that I will also rescue somebody through the same process. That is why I took the courage to become a diver
quotes.context: National Geographic 'Extreme Rescues', episode 'Sunken Survivor' (YouTube 51dzWMMDok8, uploaded 2022). Transcribed from auto-captions, which read 'a dying' for 'a diver'. Check by ear.
quotes.korean: 사람들이 알았으면 해요. 저는 제 두려움을 두려워하지 않는다는 걸요… 언젠가 저도 같은 과정을 통해 누군가를 구하게 될 거라고 마음속으로 믿어요. 그래서 용기를 내 잠수사가 됐어요.

quotes.speaker: Surface dive supervisor (Colby Werrett, DCN)
quotes.words_en: All right, you found one, yeah?
quotes.context: Helmet-cam footage, 28 May 2013, released by DCN Diving on 2-3 Dec 2013. It is said just before the hand grabs the diver, when everyone assumed a body. AFP's transcript reads 'Ah, right. You've found one, yeah?'. The wording here is from the AP and Telegraph clip captions.
quotes.korean: 좋아, 하나 찾았구나, 응?

quotes.speaker: Rescue team voice on the dive radio (DISPUTED: surface supervisor Colby Werrett or diver Nico van Heerden)
quotes.words_en: He's alive! He's alive!
quotes.context: Helmet-cam footage, 28 May 2013, the moment the hand grips the diver's glove. AFP, AFPBB, Daily Dot and Vocal attribute it to the supervisor watching the monitors. AP (11 Dec), NBC Today, Global News and Business Insider attribute it to the diver. On screen, credit it to 'the rescue team radio' (구조팀 무전).
quotes.korean: 살아 있어! 살아 있어!

quotes.speaker: Surface dive supervisor (Colby Werrett)
quotes.words_en: OK. Keep him there. All right. Just, just hold him there, OK? Keep him there.
quotes.context: Helmet-cam footage, 28 May 2013, right after the discovery. AFP transcript. The captions read: 'Okay, keep him there. Keep him there... Hold him there, okay? Just keep him there.'
quotes.korean: 좋아. 거기 붙잡고 있어. 좋아. 그냥, 그냥 거기 잡고 있어, 알았지? 거기 붙잡고 있어.

quotes.speaker: Surface dive supervisor (Colby Werrett)
quotes.words_en: hell! I don't know what we're going to do.
quotes.context: Helmet-cam footage, 28 May 2013. AFP prints it as 'hell!'. The Daily Dot prints the full expletive: 'Fucking hell. I don't know what we're going to do now.' This is a genuine moment of shock; the profanity is best omitted, and 'I don't know what we're going to do' can be used.
quotes.korean: 젠장! 이제 어떻게 해야 할지 모르겠어.

quotes.speaker: Surface dive supervisor (Colby Werrett)
quotes.words_en: Just keep him there, keep him there. Just reassure him. Pat him on the shoulder.
quotes.context: Helmet-cam footage, 28 May 2013. NBC Today attributes it to 'the diver's colleague' and HuffPost to Werrett.
quotes.korean: 그냥 거기 붙잡고 있어, 붙잡고 있어. 그냥 안심시켜 줘. 어깨를 토닥여 줘.

quotes.speaker: Surface dive supervisor (Colby Werrett) and Harrison Okene
quotes.words_en: What's your name? / Harrison. / Okay, Harrison. My name is Colby.
quotes.context: Helmet-cam footage, 28 May 2013, once Okene had a helmet with comms. AFP reports his reply as 'Harrison, Harrison', and that he confirmed he was the cook. The 'My name is Colby' line comes from captions of three videos, not from a printed transcript.
quotes.korean: 이름이 뭐예요? / 해리슨. / 좋아요, 해리슨. 내 이름은 콜비예요.

quotes.speaker: Surface dive supervisor (Colby Werrett)
quotes.words_en: Can you hear me? ... OK, listen to me, we're putting the hood on so you can breathe. You mustn't panic, all right? We're going to bring you home, OK?
quotes.context: Helmet-cam footage, 28 May 2013, as the diving helmet is fitted. This is AFP's transcript and AFPBB matches it. HuffPost gives 'You mustn't panic, you must listen to me.' The DCN full-video captions read 'listen to me ... you mustn't panic ... we're gonna bring you home'.
quotes.korean: 들려요? … 좋아요, 내 말 들어요. 숨 쉴 수 있게 후드를 씌우고 있어요. 당황하면 안 돼요, 알았죠? 우리가 집에 데려다줄게요, 알았죠?

quotes.speaker: Surface dive supervisor (Colby Werrett)
quotes.words_en: What we want you to do is keep calm, OK? Are you feeling OK? Are you sure? Have got any injuries?
quotes.context: Helmet-cam footage, 28 May 2013. AFP transcript. The captions hear 'Are you sore? Have you got any injuries?', so 'sure' versus 'sore' is uncertain.
quotes.korean: 침착하게 있어 줘요, 알았죠? 괜찮아요? 확실해요?(또는: 아픈 데 있어요?) 다친 데 있어요?

quotes.speaker: Surface dive supervisor (Colby Werrett)
quotes.words_en: Let's get that hat on his head so we can reduce the CO2, please.
quotes.context: Helmet-cam footage, 28 May 2013. Divers call the helmet a 'hat'. Machine captions only, from two separate videos (Telegraph clip and NatGeo).
quotes.korean: 이산화탄소를 줄일 수 있게, 그 헬멧을 그의 머리에 씌우자.

quotes.speaker: Surface dive supervisor (Colby Werrett)
quotes.words_en: Good job, my friend. Well done. You're a survivor!
quotes.context: Helmet-cam footage, 28 May 2013, when Okene was pulled into the diving bell. AFP transcript, and the AFPBB Japanese version matches.
quotes.korean: 잘했어요, 친구. 정말 잘했어요. 당신은 생존자예요!

quotes.speaker: Voice on the dive radio (diver or supervisor)
quotes.words_en: Drink it, buddy. Drink it.
quotes.context: Helmet-cam footage, 28 May 2013, as Okene sips bottled water. Machine captions of the AP clip only.
quotes.korean: 마셔요, 친구. 마셔요.

quotes.speaker: Nico van Heerden (diver), as reported by HuffPost
quotes.words_en: There's someone in the water
quotes.context: HuffPost (Dec 2013) says Van Heerden says this at about 5:30 of the DCN video. It does not appear in any available captions or in AFP's transcript.
quotes.korean: 물속에 누가 있어.

quotes.speaker: DCN Diving (company email to AFP)
quotes.words_en: tribute to us all working on this amazing rescue
quotes.context: December 2013. DCN's reason for releasing the nearly 11-minute helmet-cam video.
quotes.korean: 이 놀라운 구조 작업에 함께한 우리 모두에게 바치는 헌사

quotes.speaker: Tony Walker (project manager, DCN Diving)
quotes.words_en: The diver acknowledged that he had seen the hand and then, when he went to grab the hand, the hand grabbed him!
quotes.context: AP telephone interview, Tuesday 3 Dec 2013. Walker was watching the diver's camera feed on a screen in the control room.
quotes.korean: 잠수부는 손을 봤다고 알렸어요. 그리고 그 손을 잡으려는 순간, 그 손이 그를 붙잡았어요!

quotes.speaker: Tony Walker (DCN Diving)
quotes.words_en: It was frightening for everybody. For the guy that was trapped because he didn't know what was happening. It was a shock for the diver while he was down there looking for bodies, and we (in the control room) shot back when the hand grabbed him on the screen.
quotes.context: AP telephone interview, 3 Dec 2013.
quotes.korean: 모두에게 무서운 순간이었어요. 갇혀 있던 사람은 무슨 일이 벌어지는지 몰랐으니까요. 시신을 찾으러 내려가 있던 잠수부에게도 충격이었고, (통제실에 있던) 우리는 화면 속에서 그 손이 그를 붙잡는 순간 뒤로 몸을 젖혔어요.

quotes.speaker: Tony Walker (DCN Diving)
quotes.words_en: He was incredibly lucky he was in an air pocket but he would have had a limited time (before) ... he wouldn't be able to breathe anymore.
quotes.context: AP telephone interview, 3 Dec 2013, on how long Okene could have lasted.
quotes.korean: 공기주머니 안에 있었던 건 엄청난 행운이었지만, 그에게 남은 시간은 한정돼 있었어요… 더 이상 숨을 쉴 수 없게 되기까지는요.

quotes.speaker: Jed Chamberlain (manager, DCN Global, Abu Dhabi)
quotes.words_en: We located the Jascon-4, which lay upside down on the sea bed at 30 metres. At the time, there was no trace of crew members and little hope of finding survivors. The divers entered the vessel to retrieve bodies of the crew members. Amazingly, the recovery mission turned into a rescue mission.
quotes.context: The National (UAE), Jennifer Bell, 13 June 2013 (he spoke 'yesterday', i.e. 12 June).
quotes.korean: 우리는 수심 30m 해저에 뒤집힌 채 놓인 Jascon-4를 찾아냈습니다. 당시에는 선원들의 흔적이 없었고, 생존자를 찾을 희망도 거의 없었습니다. 잠수부들은 선원들의 시신을 수습하러 선내로 들어갔습니다. 놀랍게도, 시신 수습 작업이 구조 작업으로 바뀌었습니다.

quotes.speaker: Jed Chamberlain (DCN Global)
quotes.words_en: It was incredible. They thought they were just looking for bodies.
quotes.context: The National (UAE), 13 June 2013.
quotes.korean: 믿기지 않는 일이었어요. 그들은 그저 시신을 찾고 있는 줄 알았거든요.

quotes.speaker: Jed Chamberlain (DCN Global)
quotes.words_en: Amazingly, after two to three days, he was absolutely fine.
quotes.context: The National (UAE), 13 June 2013, about the decompression chamber.
quotes.korean: 놀랍게도, 이삼일 뒤 그는 완전히 괜찮았어요.

quotes.speaker: Jed Chamberlain (commercial manager, DCN Global)
quotes.words_en: Needless to say, the diver got quite a fright.
quotes.context: Told to the BBC in Dec 2013, quoted by Global News. Chamberlain also told the BBC that Okene was 'absolutely calm' and that 'You don't hear about stories like this very often.' The BBC original was not retrieved.
quotes.korean: 말할 것도 없이, 잠수부는 꽤 놀랐죠.

quotes.speaker: West African Ventures (Jascon-4 operator), statement
quotes.words_en: Our divers performed an extremely difficult and dangerous task in the most testing of conditions. We are grateful for their professional service, as well as the contributions of many other personnel who gave all their efforts to this challenging recovery operation. Mr Harrison Okene has been brought to the surface safely and he continues to respond to treatment.
quotes.context: Statement in early June 2013, when the search for the last missing crew member was called off. The National quotes a second line: 'The vessel has become so unstable that the risk of injury to our rescue divers has become unacceptably high.'
quotes.korean: 우리 잠수부들은 가장 혹독한 조건에서 극도로 어렵고 위험한 임무를 수행했습니다. 그들의 전문적인 노고와, 이 힘든 수습 작업에 온 힘을 쏟은 다른 많은 인원들의 기여에 감사드립니다. 해리슨 오케네 씨는 무사히 수면으로 올라왔으며 계속 치료에 반응하고 있습니다.

quotes.speaker: Kurt Glaubitz (Chevron spokesman)
quotes.words_en: Initial reports indicated that heavy ocean swells caused the Jascon 4 to capsize, while performing tension tow operations of the tanker.
quotes.context: Chevron statement, late May or June 2013.
quotes.korean: 초기 보고에 따르면, Jascon 4는 유조선 장력 예인 작업을 하던 중 거센 너울 때문에 전복됐습니다.

quotes.speaker: Paul MacDonald (officer on the dive support vessel), Facebook post
quotes.words_en: The diver walked in and at the back there was an air pocket he was sitting in. How it wasn't full of water is anyone's guess. I would say someone was looking after him.
quotes.context: Facebook post soon after the rescue, quoted by The Guardian around 13 June 2013. The Telegraph spells the name 'Paul McDonald'.
reported_by: Taipei Times reprint of The Guardian
quotes.korean: 잠수부가 들어가 보니 안쪽에 공기주머니가 있었고, 그가 거기 앉아 있었습니다. 그곳이 어떻게 물로 가득 차지 않았는지는 아무도 모릅니다. 누군가 그를 지켜 주고 있었다고 말하고 싶네요.

quotes.speaker: Paul McDonald (member of the rescue crew)
quotes.words_en: All on board could not believe how cool he was when being rescued. The divers put a diving helmet and harness onto him. It was amazing to be part of this rescue.
quotes.context: The Telegraph, 12 June 2013. The Daily Mail used the same quote.
reported_by: News Express Nigeria ('Text courtesy Daily Mail')
quotes.korean: 구조되는 동안 그가 얼마나 침착했는지, 배에 있던 모두가 믿지 못했습니다. 잠수부들이 그에게 잠수 헬멧과 하네스를 씌웠어요. 이 구조에 함께했다는 게 놀라운 일이었습니다.

quotes.speaker: Nico van Heerden (DCN saturation diver who found Okene, 32, Strand, South Africa)
quotes.words_en: I got a huge fright but was relieved to find someone alive
quotes.context: A message he sent to his wife Simoné, reported by the Cape Times in June 2013 and quoted by Soundings in Dec 2013. The Cape Times original (IOL) was blocked.
quotes.korean: 엄청 놀랐지만, 살아 있는 사람을 찾아서 안도했어.

quotes.speaker: Simoné van Heerden (wife of diver Nico van Heerden)
quotes.words_en: It took him three hours to open one door. There was one body. He found another two bodies. ... When he turned around and saw that guy's face … that feeling can't be explained.
quotes.context: Cape Times, June 2013, quoted by Soundings. NatGeo's documentary has Nico saying it took 'about two and a half hours' to break one door down.
quotes.korean: 문 하나 여는 데 세 시간이 걸렸대요. 시신이 하나 있었고, 시신 두 구를 더 찾았어요. … 돌아섰을 때 그 사람 얼굴을 봤는데… 그 기분은 설명할 수가 없대요.

quotes.speaker: Nico van Heerden (diver), in NatGeo 'Extreme Rescues'
quotes.words_en: I think I was a bit in shock. I was frozen there for a minute or two.
quotes.context: Interview in the NatGeo 'Sunken Survivor' episode (YouTube 51dzWMMDok8), about the discovery. Transcribed from auto-captions, and the speaker is inferred from context. Check by ear.
quotes.korean: 제가 좀 충격을 받았던 것 같아요. 1~2분 동안 그 자리에 얼어붙어 있었어요.

quotes.speaker: Alex Gibbs (life support technician on duty)
quotes.words_en: I was shocked and then a bit excited. Nobody thought there was anyone alive.
quotes.context: 9News (Australia, 2022), quoted by LADbible on 31 Aug 2023.
quotes.korean: 처음엔 충격이었고, 그다음엔 조금 들떴어요. 살아 있는 사람이 있을 거라고는 아무도 생각하지 않았거든요.

quotes.speaker: Alex Gibbs (life support technician)
quotes.words_en: Contrary to popular belief, when people are trapped in confined spaces it is not the oxygen running out that will kill you, it is your own exhaled breath causing a build-up of CO2. By the time he had been found, this was at a clearly high level. You can see him panting in the video and his slightly glazed eyes caused by this.
quotes.context: 9News (2022), via LADbible 2023. Useful to explain the CO2 danger.
quotes.korean: 흔히 생각하는 것과 달리, 좁은 공간에 갇혔을 때 사람을 죽이는 건 산소 고갈이 아니라, 자기가 내쉰 숨 때문에 쌓이는 이산화탄소입니다. 그가 발견됐을 때 그 수치는 분명히 높았어요. 영상에서 그가 헐떡이는 모습과, 그 때문에 약간 흐릿해진 눈을 볼 수 있습니다.

quotes.speaker: Eric Hexdall (clinical director of diving medicine, Duke Center for Hyperbaric Medicine)
quotes.words_en: If you're trapped in something like that, your carbon dioxide levels will build to a toxic level before you use up the oxygen
quotes.context: National Geographic, 4 Dec 2013. His estimate assumed a pocket of about 13.5 m3: CO2 symptoms at about 56 hours and unconsciousness at about 79 hours. These are modelled estimates, not measurements.
quotes.korean: 그런 곳에 갇히면, 산소를 다 쓰기 전에 이산화탄소 농도가 먼저 독성 수준까지 올라갑니다.

quotes.speaker: Petar Denoble (VP of research, Divers Alert Network)
quotes.words_en: He can't come back to the surface immediately. If he did, he would die.
quotes.context: National Geographic, 4 Dec 2013, explaining why decompression was needed.
quotes.korean: 그는 곧바로 수면으로 올라올 수 없습니다. 그랬다면 죽었을 겁니다.

quotes.notes:
I collected 78 quotes. Below: what is solid, what is disputed, what to leave out, and the number checks.

SOURCE TIERS
- Best: Reuters (Joe Brock, Warri, 12 Jun 2013); AP (3 Dec 2013, and Sunday Alamba's 11 Dec 2013 interview); AFP (Dec 2013, its transcript of the footage); The Telegraph (12 Jun 2013, which reprints The Nation interview); The Guardian (13 Jun 2013); The National UAE (13 Jun 2013, DCN's Jed Chamberlain); National Geographic (Dec 2013).
- Could not open the originals: The Nation (Nigeria) 2013 interview, the Guardian 2023 feature by Paula Cocozza, the Cape Times June 2013 article, the BBC 2013 piece, and the BBC World Service 'Lives Less Ordinary' episode 'Miracle on the ocean floor' (Aug 2023; no transcript online). Those quotes come from consistent reprints and are labelled.
- Machine captions (marked 'paraphrase'): the AP on-camera interview (YouTube xrO2ENzr2cM), the NatGeo 'Extreme Rescues' episode (51dzWMMDok8), and the 2024 faith-channel testimony (rkPT4j4CuXA). Listen and check before putting these on screen as quotes.
- Saved caption files: /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-aireels/82e206d8-83ed-5019-be3d-65c96a1bf62c/scratchpad/okene/yt/ (natgeo.txt, testimony.txt, *.vtt). Only captions were downloaded, no media.

FOOTAGE LINES NOT FOUND
- 'Come, come, come' and 'I'm going to put the harness on you' are not in AFP's transcript, the AP, Telegraph or DCN video captions, or any article. Do not use them.
- 'corpse, corpse, a corpse' is only Okene's memory, reported by AP. The audible line is the supervisor asking 'you found one, yeah?'.
- Who shouted 'He's alive!' is disputed (supervisor Colby Werrett vs diver Nico van Heerden). Credit it to 'the rescue team radio' (구조팀 무전).
- The original full video is DCN's own: about 10:42 on YouTube 2FkbfMk0wCI, 'nearly 11 minutes' per AFP.

DO NOT USE
- 'After you get used to living in freezing, pitch-black, air-pocket conditions...' comes from The Beaverton, a satire site. It is not a real quote.
- His 2024 testimony blames the chief mate for not sounding the alarm. That is an unverified accusation against a dead crew member.
- His 2024 testimony also describes touching his colleagues' swollen bodies. Leave it out.
- I recommend leaving out the Reuters lines about fish eating the bodies and the smell of the dead, out of respect for the families.
- The 'black magic' accusation is sensitive; skip it.

NUMBERS (checked)
- Capsize: Sunday 26 May 2013, before dawn. Reuters gives 04:50, AP and Slate about 04:30, the Guardian and Telegraph about 05:00. Use '새벽 5시 무렵' (around 5 a.m.).
- Location: Escravos area, Gulf of Guinea. Reuters says about 30 km / 20 miles offshore; the Guardian's '12 miles (20 km)' is inconsistent. The tug was doing a tension tow for a Chevron tanker at a Chevron platform.
- Depth: 30 m, about 100 ft (company, via Reuters and Chamberlain). Okene said 33 m in 2024.
- Crew: 12 aboard, 11 died, 10 bodies recovered and 1 never found. The 12 were 11 Nigerians (Okene included) and a Ukrainian captain, with four cadets from Nigeria's Maritime Academy among them. When Okene was found, 4 bodies had been recovered (AP and Walker). The Telegraph's 'found ten of the 11 bodies' first gets the order wrong.
- Time trapped: about 60-62 hours. From the capsize at about 04:50 on 26 May to surfacing in the diving bell at 19:32 on Tuesday 28 May (Reuters) is about 62.7 hours; AFP and the Cape Times say 62. AP's '72 hours' and the common 'three days' are overstated. Use '약 60시간'.
- Decompression: about 60 hours per Okene to Reuters; 2.5 days per Chamberlain to the BBC; 'two to three days' per Chamberlain to The National; '3 days' per Okene in 2024. Use '약 60시간(2.5일)'.
- Air pocket: Reuters says 'four foot high' and the toilet 'four foot square'; the Guardian says '4ft sq'. NatGeo's 13.5 m3 is an assumption in Hexdall's model, not a measurement. Physicist Umansky estimated about 6 m3 of compressed air was needed and guessed the pocket connected to a larger one.
- Temperature: no measured figure exists. AP's 'temperature dropped to freezing' is unsupported for tropical Gulf of Guinea water. Okene's own words are 'very, very cold'. Do not say 'freezing' or give a °C value.
- Food and water: Reuters says nothing to eat or drink. AP says one bottle of Coke. His 2024 testimony mentions a Coke and a can of sardines. Use '콜라 한 병' (one bottle of Coke), labelled as his account, or skip it.
- Light: he found a life vest with two small flashlights, which died in under a day (AP).
- Age: 29. Wife: Akpovona (AP), 'Akpos' (Telegraph).
- Rescuers: DCN Diving (AP calls it Dutch; The National calls it DCN Global, Emirati-owned, Mussafah, Abu Dhabi). Saturation divers were Nico van Heerden, Darryl Oosthuizen and André Erasmus; the surface supervisor was Colby Werrett. They worked from the dive support vessel Lewek Toucan, chartered by West African Ventures and about 17 hours away (Chamberlain) or 120 km away (Walker).
- Dates: the rescue footage was released on 2-3 Dec 2013, about six months later. Some AP photo captions wrongly say 'June 2013'.
- Ambiguous: the 'stars in the sky' quote and the 'surfaced at 19:32' time. He was under pressure in the bell and chamber, so when he actually saw the sky is unclear. Don't build the timeline on it.

AFTERMATH
- In 2013 he vowed never to return to the sea and took a cook's job on land.
- In June 2015 he trained as a commercial diver in South Africa. ExplorersWeb and Unilad say the diver who found him presented his diploma (secondary sources only).
- By 2022-23 he was an IMCA Class Two commercial air diver (LADbible citing 9News).

candidates.logline_ko: 2012년 9월 18일 밤, 북해 수심 약 90~100m. 지원선 Bibby Topaz의 위치유지(DP) 시스템이 고장 나 배가 거친 바다로 떠밀려 가면서, 포화잠수사 크리스 레먼스의 생명줄(엄빌리컬: 호흡가스·온수·조명 전원·통신)이 끊어진다. 등에 멘 비상가스는 약 5분 분량. 불빛 하나 없는 해저에서 그는 작업 구조물(매니폴드) 위로 올라가 몸을 고정한 뒤 의식을 잃는다. 배가 제자리로 돌아오고, ROV가 그를 찾아내고, 동료 데이브 유아사가 그를 벨로 끌어올리기까지 약 30분(당시와 2025년 일부 보도는 '거의 40분'). 벨 안에서 던컨 올콕의 인공호흡 몇 번 만에 그는 숨을 되찾았고, 약 3주 뒤 다시 바다로 내려갔다.
candidates.why_fits: Paria(2022)와 Okene(2013)와 같은 상업잠수·해양석유 현장이다. 생명줄, 어둠, 남은 가스량이라는 같은 장치가 이어져 '바다 밑 생존' 3부작이 된다. 비상가스 5분과 실제 고립 30분 이상의 격차가 그대로 카운트다운 구조가 되어 90초 안에 숨막히는 긴장을 만든다. 사망자가 없고 당사자들이 살아서 공개 인터뷰를 여러 번 했기 때문에 실명 인용 카드를 만들기 쉽다. 결말의 '왜 살았나'(차가운 수온과 높은 산소분압 가설)는 반전이 되지만, 반드시 '추정'으로 표기해야 한다. Paria의 비극 다음에 오는 '기적' 편이라 시리즈의 감정 균형도 맞는다.

candidates.case: 2위 · Apollo 13 — 서비스모듈 산소탱크 폭발과 달착륙선 '구명보트' 귀환
candidates.logline_ko: 1970년 4월 13일 밤 9시 7분(휴스턴 시각, 비행경과시간 55:54:53 기준 계산값), 지구에서 약 32만 km. 아폴로 13호의 산소탱크가 폭발한다. 26초 뒤 잭 스와이거트가 말한다. 'Okay, Houston... we've had a problem here.' 짐 러벨이 이어 말한다. 'Houston, we've had a problem.' 영화 속 'we have a problem'과는 다른 문장이다. 달 착륙은 취소되고, 세 사람은 2인용 달착륙선을 구명보트 삼아 전기·물·열을 아끼며 냉장고처럼 차가운 선실에서 나흘을 버틴다. 이산화탄소가 차오르자 지상팀은 사각 필터를 원형 소켓에 맞추는 임시 장치('우편함')의 제작법을 무선으로 불러준다. 4월 17일, 세 사람 모두 태평양에 착수한다.
candidates.why_fits: 갇힌 공간, 줄어드는 생명유지 자원(전력·산소·CO2·추위), 시간과의 싸움, 전원 생존이라는 구성이 Okene 편과 같다. 후보 가운데 유일하게 실제 음성(1970년 공대지 교신 원본)을 허가 없이 쓸 수 있는 퍼블릭 도메인 사건이라, '우리는 제3자 음원을 쓰지 않는다' 원칙을 지키면서 진짜 목소리를 넣을 수 있다. '영화 대사는 틀렸다'는 첫 3초 훅이 강하다. 비행경과시간이 초 단위로 남아 있어 '누가, 언제, 무엇을 말했나'를 완벽히 검증할 수 있다.

candidates.sensitivities: 118명 전원 사망이라 가장 무겁다. 사망 순간이나 질식 과정을 연출하지 말고, 쪽지 문장과 빈 구획 일러스트로 여백을 남긴다. 2000년 유족 간담회에서 어머니 나데즈다 틸릭이 진정제를 맞는 장면이 유명하지만, 이를 묘사하거나 언급하는 것은 금지. 쪽지 문구는 번역본마다 다르므로(예: 'writing blind' / 'by feel') 러시아어 원문 기준으로 번역할 것. 시각 분쟁도 표기한다(쪽지 13:15·15:45 vs 해군 발표 13:34~15:15). 수심 108m는 널리 인용되지만 이번 조사에서 1차 출처로 확인하지 못했다. 침몰 원인은 러시아 공식 결론(연습어뢰 과산화수소 누출·폭발)과 충돌설이 엇갈리므로 공식 결론으로 서술하고 이견이 있음을 밝힌다. 한국 시청자에게는 '가라앉은 배, 늦은 구조, 분노한 유족'이 세월호를 연상시킬 수 있으니 직접 비교 없이 절제할 것. 댓글 관리도 필요.
candidates.legal_risk: 낮음~중간. 공개 사실 위주이고 사인(私人)을 겨냥하지 않는다. 러시아 정부의 대응을 비판하는 것은 기록된 사실(외국 지원 수용 시점, 공식 발표)로 한정한다. 실제 유족이나 승조원의 얼굴 묘사는 금지.

candidates.logline_ko: 2010년 8월 5일, 칠레 산호세 구리·금 광산이 무너진다. 광부 33명이 지하 약 700m 대피소에 갇힌다. 17일 동안 지상은 그들이 살아 있는지조차 몰랐다. 8월 22일 오후 3시 17분, 탐사 드릴 끝에 테이프로 붙어 올라온 종이 한 장. 'Estamos bien en el refugio los 33.'(우리 33명은 대피소에서 무사하다.) 그로부터 52일 뒤, 구조 캡슐 '페닉스(Fénix)'가 한 명씩 끌어올려 10월 13일 밤 마지막 반장 루이스 우르수아까지 33명 전원이 지상에 섰다. 갇힌 지 69일 만이었다.
candidates.why_fits: '갇힘, 침묵, 생존 신호, 시간과의 구조전'이라는 장르의 정석이고 전원 생존이다. 17일간의 침묵이 숨막히는 중반부를 만들고, 손글씨 쪽지(실존 문장, 작성자와 시각 확인됨)가 꾸며낸 대사 없이 클라이맥스가 된다. 한국에도 잘 알려진 사건이지만 국내 사건이 아니라서 부담이 적다.

candidates.public_domain_audio: 없음. 칠레 정부와 TVN의 구조 생중계 영상, 피녜라 대통령이 쪽지를 낭독하는 영상은 저작권을 확인하지 못했으므로 사용 금지. 쪽지 실물은 박물관 소장품이라 사진 대신 직접 그린 재현 일러스트로 쓰고, 문구는 짧게 인용하며 출처를 표기한다. 2015년 영화 'The 33'(Warner) 자료는 사용 금지.
candidates.sensitivities: 사망자는 없지만 후유증이 크다. 다수가 PTSD, 생계난, 소송을 겪었고, 쪽지 작성자 호세 오헤다는 2017년 정신과 입원 보도가 있었다. '해피엔딩'으로만 포장하지 말고 소비하지도 말 것. 광산 소유주(San Esteban)의 안전 위반 문제는 법원·정부 기록 범위에서만 언급한다. 숫자 분쟁을 표기할 것: 대피소 깊이 약 700m vs 구조 갱도 약 622m(2,041피트), 69일 vs '70일'. 우르수아의 탈출 시각도 21:55~21:58로 출처마다 다르다. 지하에서 33명이 나눈 대화를 재구성하는 것은 금지. 본인들이 이후 인터뷰에서 직접 한 말만 쓴다.
candidates.legal_risk: 낮음. 공개 사실이고 생존자를 긍정적으로 다룬다. 영화·방송 영상과 실물 사진을 쓰지 않고, 실존 광부 얼굴을 닮게 그리지 않는다는 조건에서.

candidates.case: 예비 5 · 태국 탐루엉 동굴 구조 (Wild Boars 축구팀)
candidates.logline_ko: 2018년 6월 23일, 유소년 축구팀 12명과 코치가 동굴에 들어간 뒤 불어난 물에 갇힌다. 7월 2일 밤, 영국 동굴잠수사 존 볼랜선과 릭 스탠턴이 진흙 둔덕 위에서 그들을 찾는다. 'How many of you?' 'Thirteen.' 'Brilliant.' 산소통을 나르던 전 태국 해군 특수부대원 사만 쿠난이 7월 6일 숨지고, 7월 8~10일 진정 상태의 아이들을 한 명씩 잠수로 끌고 나와 13명 전원이 구조된다.
candidates.why_fits: 물에 잠긴 좁은 동굴(잠수와 폐소), 산소 수치 하락, 우기 전 시간과의 싸움이 Okene, Lemons와 같은 결이다. 실제 주고받은 짧은 대화가 영상으로 기록되어 있어 인용 카드로 쓰기 좋다.

candidates.sensitivities: 구조 당시 아이들은 미성년자였고, 이야기 판권이 '13 Tham Luang' 회사와 넷플릭스에 묶여 아이들의 인터뷰가 제한된다. 관련 사망자가 3명이다: 사만 쿠난(2018-07-06), 해군 특수부대원 베이룻 팍바라(2019, 구조 중 감염 합병증), 생존자 둥펫 '돔' 프롬텝(2023-02, 영국에서 사망). 진정제 투여 관련 내용은 정확히 다뤄야 한다. 대화의 화자가 출처마다 엇갈리므로(질문한 사람이 볼랜선인지) 책으로 검증할 것. 한국 시청자가 이미 여러 콘텐츠로 많이 접해 신선도가 낮다.
candidates.legal_risk: 중간. 사실 보도 범위는 문제없지만, 아이들의 얼굴·이름을 강조하면 판권과 사생활 문제가 생긴다. 실루엣과 잠수사 위주로 구성해야 한다.

candidates.case: 예비 6 · OceanGate 'Titan' 잠수정 내파 (타이태닉 잔해 탐사)
candidates.country_year: 북대서양(미국 기업, 캐나다 지원선 Polar Prince) / 2023-06-18
candidates.logline_ko: 2023년 6월 18일, 탄소섬유 선체의 잠수정 '타이탄'이 5명을 태우고 수심 약 3,800m의 타이태닉 잔해를 향해 내려간다. 수심 약 2,274m에서 보낸 문자는 'All good here.', 약 3,341m에서 보낸 마지막 문자는 'Dropped two wts.'(추 두 개 투하). 수심 약 3,346m에서 통신이 끊긴다. 세계가 나흘 동안 '남은 산소'를 세는 사이, 잠수정은 이미 사라진 뒤였다. 2025년 8월 미국 해안경비대 조사위원회는 결론을 내렸다. '예방할 수 있었다.'
candidates.why_fits: 폐소, 심해, 카운트다운, 그리고 명백한 과실이라는 축이 Paria 편(과실)과 이어진다. 미국 해안경비대(USCG) 해양사고조사위원회의 청문 자료와 최종보고서가 미국 정부저작물이라, 실제 문자 로그와 조사 결론을 허가 없이 인용할 수 있다.

candidates.public_domain_audio: 부분적으로 있음. USCG 최종보고서, 청문회 전시자료(문자 로그 애니메이션 포함), USCG가 공개한 청문 영상은 미국 연방정부 저작물(PD)이다. 다만 증인 증언 음성은 실존 개인의 목소리라 퍼블리시티 문제가 생길 수 있으니 텍스트로만 쓰는 것을 권장한다. USCG의 잔해 영상에는 유해 관련 장면이 있을 수 있으므로 사용 금지. 다큐(넷플릭스 등) 자료도 사용 금지.
candidates.sensitivities: 사건이 너무 최근이다(3년). 사망자 5명 중 술레만 다우드는 당시 19세였다. 사건 당시 조롱 밈이 퍼졌으므로 조롱 톤은 절대 금지. '쾅쾅거리는 소리'나 '남은 산소 96시간' 같은 수색 당시 추측성 보도를 사실처럼 쓰면 안 된다. 실제로는 조사에서 통신 두절 시점에 내파된 것으로 본다. 과실 서술은 USCG 보고서 문구로만 한정한다.
candidates.legal_risk: 중간. 유족 소송이 진행 중이다(나르졸레 유족이 2024년 OceanGate를 상대로 5천만 달러 소송). 고인 스톡턴 러시와 회사 관계자에 대한 과실 단정은 반드시 USCG 결론을 그대로 인용하는 방식으로만 쓴다.

cands.ranking_notes:
순위 요약: 1) Chris Lemons(9.0) 2) Apollo 13(8.5) 3) Kursk(8.5) 4) 칠레 33인(8.0). 이 4건이 요청한 다음 작업 큐다. 5·6위(탐루엉 7.5, Titan 7.0)는 예비 후보다.

순위 근거:
- Lemons를 1위로 둔 이유: Paria, Okene와 같은 상업잠수 세계라 '바다 밑' 시리즈가 자연스럽게 이어지고, 전원 생존이라 윤리 부담이 가장 작다. '비상가스 5분 vs 고립 약 30분'이 그대로 90초 카운트다운 구조가 된다.
- Apollo 13과 Kursk는 동점이다. Apollo 13을 앞에 둔 이유는 유일하게 퍼블릭 도메인 실제 음성(NASA 공대지 교신)을 허가 없이 넣을 수 있고, 사망자가 없으며, 모든 발언을 비행경과시간 초 단위로 검증할 수 있어서다. Kursk는 주제상 Okene와 가장 닮은 쌍둥이(가라앉은 선체, 밀폐 구획, 결말만 반대)지만 118명 사망과 세월호 연상 위험 때문에 반 단계 뒤로 놓았다. 다만 Okene 편 바로 다음에 올리면 대비 효과는 Kursk가 가장 크다.
- 칠레는 전원 생존에 실존 쪽지까지 있어 강력하지만, 69일을 90초로 압축하기 어렵고 생존자들의 이후 고통이 커서 4위로 두었다.

탈락·보류:
- Nutty Putty(2009): 시신이 아직 동굴에 있고 사망 과정 자체가 중심이며 인터넷 밈화가 심하다. 유족 존중 기준에 맞지 않아 제외.
- Byford Dolphin(1983): 고어를 피할 수 없어 제외.
- 추가 예비 후보 1, USS Squalus(1939, 미국): 26명 사망, McCann 구조챔버로 33명을 구조한 최초의 심해 잠수함 구조. 수심 약 243피트. 미 해군 역사기록(DANFS)과 사진이 모두 PD다.
- 추가 예비 후보 2, Sago 탄광(2006, 미국): 13명이 갇혀 1명 생존. 마틴 톨러의 쪽지 'It wasn't bad. I just went to sleep.'가 남아 있고 MSHA 보고서가 PD다. 다만 가족에게 '생존' 오보가 났던 일이 너무 잔인해 민감도가 높다.

공통 제작 원칙(모든 후보): 대사·속마음 창작 금지. 실제 말은 '누가·언제·어디서'를 붙인 텍스트 카드로만 쓴다. 영화·다큐·뉴스 영상과 음원은 쓰지 않는다. 퍼블릭 도메인 음성은 Apollo 13(NASA)과 Titan(USCG 문서)만 해당한다. 분쟁 수치는 화면에 '보도마다 다름'으로 표기한다. 실존 인물 얼굴을 닮게 그리지 않는다.

상위 작업 참고(Okene 편): 한국에서 '에어포켓'은 2014년 세월호 때 크게 논쟁된 단어다. Okene 편 내레이션이나 해시태그에서 이 단어를 쓸 때는 세월호와 직접 비교하지 말고, 댓글 반응도 염두에 둘 것.

미검증 항목(제작 전 확인 필요): Lemons 직접 인용문(CBC 인터뷰가 403으로 열리지 않음. 다큐에서 전사 필요), Apollo 13 선실 온도 38°F의 1차 출처, Kursk 수심 108m와 콜레스니코프 쪽지 러시아어 원문, 프레드 헤이즈 생존 여부, Lemons 다큐·영화의 한국 개봉 여부.

draft.caption_ko:
[실화] 수심 30m, 뒤집힌 배 속에서 60시간을 버틴 요리사
※ 실제 영상과 음성은 쓰지 않았습니다. 증언과 무전 내용은 언론 보도를 글자로 옮겼습니다.

2013년 5월 26일 새벽, 나이지리아 에스크라보스 앞바다 약 30km 해상에서 일어난 일입니다. 시각은 본인 진술로 4시 50분이고, AP는 4시 30분경으로 보도했습니다. 셰브런의 원유 선적 부이에서 유조선을 붙잡던 예인선 재스콘 4호(운영사 West African Ventures)가 뒤집혔고, 거꾸로 엎어진 채 수심 약 30m 해저로 가라앉았습니다. 셰브런은 초기 보고에서 거센 너울을 원인으로 들었습니다. 공개된 최종 조사 결과는 찾지 못했습니다.

승선 12명 가운데 요리사 해리슨 오케네(당시 29세)는 사관 선실 옆 작은 화장실과 그 옆 선실에 남은 공기주머니에서 어둠과 추위, 갈증을 견뎠습니다. 로이터 보도에 따르면 공기층 높이는 약 1.2m였습니다. 5월 28일 오후, 시신을 수습하러 투입된 DCN 다이빙 포화잠수팀이 그를 찾아냈습니다. 그는 헬멧을 쓰고 잠수종으로 옮겨졌고, 감압 챔버에서 약 60시간(보도에 따라 2~3일) 동안 감압을 받았습니다.

선장을 포함한 11명이 숨졌습니다. 10명의 시신은 수습됐고 1명은 찾지 못했습니다. 선체가 불안정해 5월 31일 수색이 중단됐습니다.

오케네는 2013년 "다시는 바다에 가지 않겠다"고 말했습니다. 하지만 2015년 남아공에서 상업 잠수 과정을 마쳤고, 2022~23년 인터뷰 당시 상업 잠수사로 일하고 있었습니다.

숫자 메모: 갇혀 있던 시간은 로이터와 본인 진술로 '60시간 이상', DCN 발표로 62시간입니다. 흔히 보이는 '72시간·3일'은 반올림한 숫자입니다. 수온은 기록이 없습니다. '콜라 한 병으로 버텼다'는 이야기는 보도마다 다릅니다(로이터와 BBC는 먹고 마신 것이 없었다고 보도했습니다).

checks.verdict: The script is mostly accurate and carefully hedged. The verified Okene quotes match their sources: the Reuters lines in quote_dark, the AP 'Why only me?' line, and the light/hand account in the AP Dec 2013 interview. Also verified: 04:50 vs AP's 4:30, 12 aboard and 11 dead (10 bodies recovered, 1 missing), about 30 m and about 30 km, DCN's 62 h, the 60 h decompression (Reuters/AP), four bodies already recovered (AP/Walker), Lewek Toucan, Denoble's 'If he did, he would die', and Gibbs' 'clearly high' CO2 level. The Coke and water-temperature hedges are correct. Fix before rendering: (1) quote_alive gives the lines to the wrong speakers. AFP has two different surface people, and no source says 'supervisor'. (2) The 'divers' segment implies the divers made the hammering; the sources don't say who made the hammer sound he heard, and Reuters says he hammered the hull himself. (3) In the capsize, the 12 cabin lights going out one by one reads as the crew dying at the moment of capsize, Okene included. (4) 'Pale hand' should be neutral lighting, not a skin tone. (5) Several attributions are imprecise: Gibbs was not quoted via 9News, The National's 'two to three days' is about his recovery, the 2.5 days is not confirmed as a DCN figure, and the source gives no date for when the search stopped. Minor: say '약 1.2 m' and '약 4기압', drop the '만큼' causal link in 'cold', and the runtime of about 99 s is over the ~90 s target.

issues.problem: The speaker labels are not supported. AFP (Gulf Times) gives 'Ah, right. You've found one, yeah?' to 'his colleague guiding operations', who presumed another dead body. It gives 'He's alive! He's alive!' and 'Just keep him there… Just reassure him… Pat him on the shoulder' to a different person, 'his colleague watching the monitors', as one speech. NBC/TODAY (theGrio) gives 'He's alive!' to the diver and the reassure/pat lines to 'his colleague on the surface'. No source calls anyone a 'supervisor'. The card gives lines 1 and 3–4 to the same '수면 감독관', which AFP contradicts. The attribution note '(감독관/잠수부)' is also wrong: the two versions are 'colleague watching the monitors' (AFP) and 'the diver' (NBC).
issues.fix_ko: Change who for line 1 to '수면 작업 지휘 동료 (AFP)', and change who for lines 2–4 to '수면 무전'. Change the note to: "'살아 있어'·'안심시켜 줘' 화자: AFP는 모니터를 보던 수면 동료, NBC는 '살아 있어'를 잠수부로 보도". So viewers know line 1 means a body, add the chip '(시신을 찾은 줄 알고)' under line 1.

issues.problem: Placing '잠수부들이 내려왔고, 망치 소리가 들렸습니다' together suggests the divers made the hammering. Reuters only quotes 'I heard a sound of a hammer hitting the vessel. Boom, boom, boom' and does not say who made it. In Reuters, Okene then pulled a water filter off and hammered the hull himself. Global News says the divers heard hammering on the hull, i.e. his. BBC Mundo 2023 says he heard the divers breaking doors and he banged on the cabin walls. AP/The Nation says he stripped the wall to steel and banged on it with a hammer. Also, the divers had already been working in the wreck, since four bodies were recovered before he was found, so '28일 오후 내려왔고' overstates the timing.

issues.problem: 'A big swell lifts the tug and the whole frame rolls 180 degrees' shows a swell as the cause. The cause is not established. Chevron's 'heavy ocean swells' was an initial report.
